concept.title: Wi-Fi Security
concept.shortdesc: Wi-Fi security protects the wireless network, connected devices, and network data from unauthorized access.

conbody.p: The uses security controls to identify authorized devices and protect wireless communication. Configure these controls before you connect client devices to the network.

section.title: Wireless Network Protection
section.p: Wireless signals can extend beyond the boundaries of a home. A person within signal range can try to connect to an unprotected network.
Use with to protect the primary Wi-Fi network identified by .
section.note: Wireless security requires users and devices to provide the correct before they can connect to the network.
Use the strongest security mode supported by the and the client devices. Do not use an obsolete security mode to support an old device. Connect the old device to an isolated network when possible.

section.title: Security Controls
section.p: Use the following controls to secure the Wi-Fi network:

ul.li: Change the default credentials for the .
Isolate IoT devices from computers and devices that store sensitive information.
Keep the firmware on the up to date.
Review the connected-device list on the regularly.

section.title: Wi-Fi and Administrator Credentials
section.p: The Wi-Fi password and the administrator password have different purposes.
The permits a client device to connect to the wireless network. The administrator password permits an authorized user to change settings in the .
section.note: Use a different password for the Wi-Fi network and the . Do not continue to use the default passwords after the initial setup.
Do not include default passwords or operational passwords in published documentation.

section.title: Guest Network
section.p: A guest network provides Internet access to visitors without giving them access to the primary Wi-Fi network.
Use for visitor devices. Configure the guest network to prevent access to local devices and network management functions.
section.note: Give visitors the guest network password. Do not give visitors the password for .
Enable client isolation if the supports it. Client isolation can prevent guest devices from communicating with each other.

section.title: IoT Device Security
section.p: IoT devices can include cameras, speakers, sensors, appliances, and home automation devices. Some IoT devices do not support the same security features as computers and smartphones.
Connect IoT devices only when they are necessary. Change their default credentials and install available device updates.
section.note: Put IoT devices on an isolated guest or IoT network when the supports network isolation. Permit only the network access that each device requires.

section.title: Security Monitoring
section.p: Sign in to the and open the regularly. Review the list of connected devices.
Remove or block a device that you do not recognize. Change the Wi-Fi password if an unauthorized device has connected to the network.
section.note: Before you block a device, compare its device name or MAC address with your known devices. Some devices use private or randomized MAC addresses.
